The 1962 reading was established on that edition's page images rather than its text layer, cross-read against the Benziger conformed printing. Differences from the antecedent: 1862 sets a comma after 'dilecti Filii tui'; 1962 sets none.; 1862 closes the petition with a full stop, 'abundare. Qui tecum'; 1962 sets a colon, 'abundare: Qui tecum'.; Conclusion length: 1862 prints the short 'Qui tecum vivit.'; 1962 prints 'Qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitate.'; No difference of any word, and no difference of word order.. Corroboration: Venice 1570 at text-layer lines 9461-9465, reading 'Omnipotens sempiterne deus dirige actus nostros in beneplacito tuo: ut in nomine dilecti filii tui mereamur bonis operibus abundare. Per eundem.' -- note the 1570 gives a DIFFERENT conclusion family ('Per eundem') from both the 1862 and the 1962 ('Qui tecum vivit'). The same formulary is reprinted in the 1570 at the Vigil of the Epiphany, lines 10445-10449. Vatican typica 1604 at text-layer lines 12055-12063. BOTH are classified degraded-latin and their own artifact records forbid resting a claim or a negative on a raw search over them; they are offered here as corroboration only and nothing in this entry depends on them..

propers.name: Collect
propers.text:
Omnipotens sempiterne Deus, dirige actus nostros in beneplacito tuo: ut in
nomine dilecti Filii tui mereamur bonis operibus abundare: Qui tecum vivit
et regnat in unitate.

translations.caution:
A lay hand missal of the 1945 revision, printed about 1955-56, not an approved liturgical translation and never an altar book. Its Holy Week is the pre-1955 rite, its sanctoral is not the 1962 sanctoral, and its second and third orations are not those of 1962. It is carried only where a 1962 formulary is the same prayer, and nothing here may be used for recitation.
